equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs and standards-conforming async iterators; no proxies, overwritten typed-array methods, concurrent mutation/detachment, private-state reflection or prototype monkey-patching. Observable contract includes returned bytes/count, typed errors, iterator lifecycle and bounded resource ownership; it does not promise identical instruction counts for bounded empty copies. Exact promise-resolution or internal microtask scheduling is not an API guarantee.
equivalents.proof: peek() has already established length <= available. Each iteration copies min(remaining chunk bytes, requested bytes still unwritten), so written cannot exceed length. Once written equals length, any remaining valid queue entries contribute a zero-length subarray and a zero-length set at offset length. The changed OR only visits these extra zero-copy entries; it exits at queue length and does not change state or output. Re-reviewed after introducing the head cursor: the loop begins at headIndex; only indices below headIndex are cleared, so every visited entry remains defined. available equals the sum of active entries from headIndex onward, less headOffset. Prefix compaction preserves their order and these invariants. The original reasoning therefore continues to apply to the active suffix.

On success, countFrames returns only after observing end of input with no buffered bytes; reader.close has no iterator.return to invoke and cannot fail. Initializing failed to true merely routes this already-idempotent successful cleanup through the try/catch branch.

equivalents.proof: A successful count returns only after has() observes EOF and proves the remaining byte count is zero, either after the last frame or after skipTrailingMetadata, which rejects any byte left after trailing metadata. skipExactly has consumed and removed every queued chunk. The success-only close call is therefore already a no-op on all externally owned resources. The internal reader is not exposed to callers.

equivalents.proof: When fewer than four bytes remain, bytes.subarray(offset, offset + 4) is shorter than four bytes and isFreeFormatHeader returns false at its own length check, before the sample-rate byte is compared. compatible() returns false exactly as with the guard; the guard only avoids creating the short view.

equivalents.proof: tied is read only after the loop, together with bestMatches < 3. Candidates reach the comparison only with at least three matches, and bestMatches starts at 0, so the first such candidate always takes the matches > bestMatches branch, which assigns tied = false. If no candidate qualifies, bestMatches < 3 throws regardless of tied.

equivalents.proof: base = second - initialPadding, so the first chain step computes next = 0 + base + initialPadding = second and repeats the same compatible() test. An incompatible second therefore yields matches = 1, which the matches < 3 filter discards, unless the range filter already skipped it. The pre-check only avoids that work.

Any later candidate with three or more matches strictly exceeds it, replacing bestBase and resetting tied = false. After a qualifying best it neither exceeds nor equals it. If no candidate reaches three, the final bestMatches < 3 test throws. The returned base and the thrown error are unchanged.

equivalents.proof: readTagHeader throws for versions outside 2..4 and for flags outside the defined set: 0xc0 for ID3v2.2 and 0xe0 for ID3v2.3, both excluding the 0x10 footer flag. Only ID3v2.4 can reach hasFooter with flags & 0x10 set, so dropping the version test cannot change hasFooter, the bytes skipped or the footer check.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs. Out-of-range typed-array reads return undefined; isVbrHeaderFrame receives a frame-sized view from count-frames or a test-constructed buffer. The observable contract is the boolean result.
equivalents.proof: If the signature would extend past the frame, at least one compared index is out of range and reads as undefined, which never equals a character code, so every() returns false exactly as the guard does.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs. Out-of-range typed-array reads return undefined; isVbrHeaderFrame receives a frame-sized view from count-frames or a test-constructed buffer. The observable contract is the boolean result.
equivalents.proof: The results differ only when a four-byte signature ends exactly at the frame end. Every caller then needs more bytes: xingAt returns false at position + 8 > frame.length, and vbriAt at position + 26 > frame.length. isVbrHeaderFrame therefore returns false either way.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs. Out-of-range typed-array reads return undefined; isVbrHeaderFrame receives a frame-sized view from count-frames or a test-constructed buffer. The observable contract is the boolean result.
equivalents.proof: If offset - text.length exceeds the frame length, so does offset + text.length and both return false. Otherwise the mutant only removes the guard, and out-of-range signature bytes read as undefined and fail every() (see EQ-VBR-TEXT-GUARD).

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs. Out-of-range typed-array reads return undefined; isVbrHeaderFrame receives a frame-sized view from count-frames or a test-constructed buffer. The observable contract is the boolean result.
equivalents.proof: As in EQ-VBR-U32-SUBTRACT-C, write the sum as 256 * K + d with K = 65536a - 256b + c, which lies in (-2^24, 2^24). Validation passes only if K = 0, so 65536a + c = 256b. Because 256b <= 65280, a = 0, so c = 256b and therefore b = c = 0. The validated flags equal the original d; all other inputs are rejected by both.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs. Out-of-range typed-array reads return undefined; isVbrHeaderFrame receives a frame-sized view from count-frames or a test-constructed buffer. The observable contract is the boolean result.
equivalents.proof: unsigned32 feeds only (flags & ~0x0f) === 0 and then the low four bits. Write the sum as 256 * K + d with K = 65536a + 256b - c in [-255, 2^24). After >>> 0 the high 24 bits are K mod 2^24, so validation passes only if K = 0, which forces a = b = c = 0, and the value is then d, as in the original. Every other input is rejected by both. An exhaustive byte-level check found no difference.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs. Out-of-range typed-array reads return undefined; isVbrHeaderFrame receives a frame-sized view from count-frames or a test-constructed buffer. The observable contract is the boolean result.
equivalents.proof: Indexed frames are at least 96 bytes long, so only free-format frames can be this short. Missing flag bytes form a suffix that includes d, so the unsigned32 sum is NaN, NaN >>> 0 is 0, validation passes, and the final check fails: required = position + 8 exceeds frame.length. xingAt returns false as with the guard.

equivalents.proof: This check runs only after textAt has established position + 4 <= frame.length, so position - 8 > frame.length can never hold. The mutant is the guard removal analysed in EQ-XING-FLAGS-GUARD.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs. Out-of-range typed-array reads return undefined; isVbrHeaderFrame receives a frame-sized view from count-frames or a test-constructed buffer. The observable contract is the boolean result.
equivalents.proof: For 40-61 byte frames, missing bytes read as undefined and become 0 under << and |. A truncated version is 0 or a multiple of 256, never 1. A truncated entry count can be positive, but then a truncated width is 0 or a multiple of 256, outside 1..4. When every field is present, the final bound 62 + entryCount * entryWidth exceeds the length. vbriAt returns false, as with the guard.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs. Out-of-range typed-array reads return undefined; isVbrHeaderFrame receives a frame-sized view from count-frames or a test-constructed buffer. The observable contract is the boolean result.
equivalents.proof: The results differ only for a 62-byte frame. There the original continues to the final bound 62 + entryCount * entryWidth <= 62, which a positive entry count and a width of at least 1 cannot satisfy, so both return false.

equivalents.proof: This check runs only after textAt has established a frame of at least 40 bytes, so 10 > frame.length never holds. The mutant is the guard removal analysed in EQ-VBRI-LENGTH-GUARD.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs and standards-conforming async iterators; no private-state reflection, prototype monkey-patching or concurrent mutation. The observable contract includes returned bytes and counts, typed errors, iterator lifecycle and bounded live queue storage. It does not promise an exact compaction frequency, identical instruction counts, or a particular throughput measurement.
equivalents.proof: Every consumed head is cleared before headIndex advances. Replacing the empty-queue fast-path condition with false leaves an empty active suffix with headIndex equal to queued.length. A later non-empty input is pushed at that exact index, so the next active head is unchanged. The remaining threshold branch still compacts whenever 1024 consumed entries accumulate, including when the suffix is empty. All bytes, offsets, lifecycle calls and error paths are unchanged; live slots remain bounded by active chunks plus at most 1023 consumed slots. This only defers empty-array compaction.

equivalents.proof: The empty-queue branch is unchanged. For a nonempty active suffix, forcing the compaction condition true removes only cleared prefix entries and resets headIndex to zero. splice preserves the active chunks and their order; headOffset has the same value after the surrounding consume step. Immediate compaction after each completed chunk therefore preserves every public cursor result and retains no additional payload references. Live slot storage is no larger than the original. The additional bounded copying cost is outside the promised functional and memory contract and is assessed by performance measurements separately.

equivalents.proof: Changing >=1024 to >1024 delays nonempty-prefix compaction by one completed chunk. Consumed entries are still cleared immediately. Before either compaction, indexing starts at headIndex and available describes precisely the active suffix; afterward the same active suffix is moved to index zero. The public results, ownership and exceptions are identical, and at most one additional undefined slot is retained. Both variants have a constant storage bound independent of total stream length.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs and standards-conforming async iterators; no private-state reflection, prototype monkey-patching or concurrent mutation. The observable contract includes returned bytes and counts, typed errors, iterator lifecycle and bounded live queue storage. It does not promise an exact compaction frequency, identical instruction counts, or a particular throughput measurement.
equivalents.proof: headIndex starts at zero. With the mutated <1024 comparison, the first completed chunk increments it to one. If the queue empties, the unchanged empty branch resets it to zero; otherwise one is below 1024, so compaction removes the cleared prefix and resets it to zero. Induction gives the same reset on every later completed chunk. Thus this exact mutant performs eager nonempty compaction, equivalent to EQ-QUEUE-EAGER-COMPACTION for bytes, offsets, errors, lifecycle and bounded storage. It cannot reach the apparent no-compaction state at headIndex>=1024 under a single-mutant execution.
